title: Our Lady of Lourdes (11 February)
hookLine: the World Day of the Sick

cards: At Lourdes, in the south of France, the processions run in an unexpected order. At the very front, not bishops, not dignitaries: people in wheelchairs and on rolling stretchers, pushed by volunteers.
Everyone else walks behind them, the healthy following the sick. The ones most places send to the back are put first. And the whole shrine grew from a poor, sick girl gathering firewood.

teach.b: Her name was Bernadette Soubirous. She was a teenager, often sick, barely schooled, and her family was so poor they lived in a single room that had once been the town jail.

On February 11, 1858, she went with her sister and a friend to gather wood near a grotto by the river, called Massabielle. There, she said, she saw a young lady dressed in white, with a blue sash and a rosary.
Through that spring and into July, Bernadette reported the lady coming again and again, asking for prayer and penance for sinners, and for a chapel.
Once she told Bernadette to dig in the mud at the back of the grotto; a trickle came up, and it became the spring that still flows there.
On March 25, when Bernadette asked her name, the lady answered in the local dialect, in words usually given as: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette didn't know what the phrase meant.

The parish priest, who had been skeptical, did: Pope Pius IX had defined that teaching only a few years before, in 1854. The bishop approved the apparitions in 1862. Bernadette never stayed for the crowds.
She became a nun, lived quietly, and died young, still often sick. Pilgrims still come in great numbers.
The Church has formally recognized only a small number of healings there as miraculous, after long medical review, and the sick keep coming anyway, to pray, to bathe, to be put first.
In 1992 Pope John Paul II made February 11 the World Day of the Sick.

how: On February 11 Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of Lourdes and the World Day of the Sick; many parishes offer the Anointing of the Sick, and pilgrims keep coming to Lourdes itself.

games.q: you're Bernadette. the lady tells you to dig in the mud at the back of the grotto and drink. people are watching. what do you do?
o: dig with your hands until water comes.
games.why: she dug, and people laughed at her muddy face. the trickle became the spring that still flows at Lourdes.

practice: Picture one person who is ill right now, in a hospital, a care home, or at home with something long and tiring, and picture their room. Think what it would mean to them to hear from you: a visit, a call, a card, a meal at the door.
If you pray, ask Our Lady of Lourdes to be with them; if not, hold them in your attention.

wordCard.voice: Bernadette, the girl. Bernadette Soubirous, the poor, often sick teenager who reported seeing Mary at the grotto of Massabielle in 1858. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the sick come first. At Lourdes, they lead the way. Six hundred fifty days now.
